selected.title: The second point of contact
selected.texas_link: Austin startup Contoro develops robots for non-palletized trailer and shipping-container unloading.

movement.action: published a profile of Contoro industrial robotics

selected.why_today: Freshly fetched October 3rd company descriptions supply a filmable application explanation following the August 25th university profile. No October launch or independent customer result is asserted.
selected.consequence: Warehouse unloading involves robotic carton handling with remote human assistance on AI edge cases. Reliability, labor savings and injury outcomes are not independently established.
selected.application_change: A robot can grasp two available carton faces and plan movements using sensed box and wall locations, with company operators available remotely.
selected.counter_image: The illustrated carton remains supported while an unresolved edge case is directed toward remote assistance. No operator gesture or proprietary interface is invented.
selected.earned_take: The described unloading combines robotic handling with human backup.

agency.next_step: Warehouse operators can evaluate the offered commercial pilot.

filmability.viewer_question: How does a robot remove a carton when another carton blocks its top?
filmability.opening_action: Start with a reachable front face beneath a stacked carton; the upper face cannot be reached.
filmability.mechanism: Two contact faces engage the same box; arm withdraws it into free space and places it on a conveyor. Attribute operation to company description.
filmability.human_consequence: The machine performs physical carton handling; remote operators remain available when AI cannot handle an edge case. Do not depict a named injured worker or claim injury reduction.
filmability.source_limit: Company product description and self-published GIF establish advertised mechanism, not independent reliability, labor savings or October deployment. Never show an invented failure classification or proprietary control screen.
three_key_images: Stacked cartons with an inaccessible upper face
Two-part gripper contacts front plus second accessible face
Same carton leaves the stack for conveyor; disclose human assistance in narration

asset_leads.inspection: Watched native browser closeup: black vacuum plate with yellow cups engages a carton front; second plate lies over another carton face; adjacent cartons and metal container wall are visible. No whole-container completion or remote operator shown.
asset_leads.rights_basis: Company footer explicitly All Rights Reserved; no reusable license found.

action_proposals.visible_action: The same edge carton has a covered top and exposed front and side. Two vacuum plates contact front and side simultaneously, withdraw it, and carry it toward an illustrative supported conveyor. A remote-assistance boundary stays unresolved before the generic carton is released onto rollers.
action_proposals.consequence: The viewer can distinguish two-face contact and physical box handling from total autonomous operation. Warehouse crews and remote operators retain a role in the company-described workflow.
action_proposals.limits: Original generic illustration of company-described workflow. No exact Contoro machine, customer incident, measured sensor output, exact AI path, reliability, labor savings or full-trailer completion. Remote assistance is an editorial boundary, not an actual interface or observed intervention.
action_proposals.source_basis: Fetched Contoro technology text identifies simultaneous front and another accessible face, sensor geometry and condition-based paths. UT identifies box unloading. Company home and about pages describe conveyor and human backup.
